templates.scenario: You work as {role|a} at {workplace|a}. Your job needs {equipment|the}, which a coworker is using for another twenty minutes. A similar-looking tool is free, but it is not designed for this job.
templates.prompt: What is the most appropriate action?

options.text: Wait for the right tool, or ask your {lead} whether another approved option is available.
options.why: Tools are designed for specific jobs, and the wrong one can damage the work or cause an injury. A short wait or a quick question is a small cost.

options.text: Use the similar tool, since it is available now and looks close enough to do the same thing.
options.why: Looking similar is not the same as being designed for the job, and a close-enough tool can produce poor work or unsafe results.
options.misconception: A similar tool is the same as the right tool.

options.text: Ask your coworker to stop in the middle of the job and hand over {equipment|the} right now.
options.why: Interrupting someone mid-task may damage their work or cause a safety problem, and the delay is only twenty minutes.
options.misconception: My job is more important than my coworker's.

options.text: Adjust the similar tool so that it fits the job better, and then use it for the work.
options.why: Modifying a tool without approval can make it unsafe or damage it, and it changes equipment that others rely on in its original form.
options.misconception: I can customize a tool to fit my needs.

templates.principle: Use the tool designed for the job; wait or ask about approved options instead of settling for a look-alike.

templates.scenario: You work as {role|a} at {workplace|a}. You are asked to use {equipment|the}, but you have not been trained on it. {coworker} says it is easy and offers to show you quickly. Your workplace allows only trained employees to operate {equipment|the}, and your {lead} is nearby.

options.text: Say you lack that training, and ask your {lead} for training or a different assignment before using it.
options.why: The workplace allows only trained people to operate it, so the first step is to say so and get properly trained or reassigned.

options.text: Let {coworker} show you quickly and then start using it, since it sounds simple enough.
options.why: A quick demo is not the same as the workplace's training. Equipment that looks easy can still injure an untrained user.
options.misconception: If someone shows me, I am trained.

options.text: Look over the controls yourself and try it on some scrap first to see how it works.
options.why: Learning by trying on your own is risky with equipment you are not trained on, even on scrap material.
options.misconception: Practicing on scrap is a safe way to learn.

options.text: Say yes without mentioning your lack of training, so that you do not seem unwilling to help.
options.why: Saying yes to something you are not trained for puts you and others at risk. Being honest about your limits is part of doing the job safely.
options.misconception: Agreeing quickly shows I am a team player.

templates.principle: Operate equipment only after the training your workplace requires; say plainly when you have not had it.

review.notes: Workplace rule stated; no operation suggested.

templates.timing: Operating comes only after training, so stating the gap must happen first.

templates.scenario: You work as {role|a} at {workplace|a}. The manufacturer's guide for {equipment|the} lists a cleaning method that takes fifteen minutes. {coworker} uses a quicker method that is not in the guide and says it works fine.
templates.prompt: What is the most appropriate action?

options.text: Follow the manufacturer's method, and tell your {lead} if the time it takes is a concern.
options.why: The manufacturer's guide is based on how the equipment is meant to be treated. If the time is a problem, your {lead} can look at it openly.

options.text: Use {coworker}'s quicker method, since it saves time and has worked fine so far.
options.why: A method that has not caused a problem yet is not the same as one that is approved. It may wear out or damage the equipment over time.
options.misconception: If it has worked so far, it is fine.

options.text: Use the quicker method only when your {lead} is not around, so nobody has a reason to object.
options.why: Hiding a shortcut means you know it might not be accepted. If it is a better method, it should be raised openly.
options.misconception: What the supervisor does not see is not a problem.

options.text: Do half of the manufacturer's steps to save time and half of the quicker method to be balanced.
options.why: Mixing the two methods follows neither one and may skip important steps in each.
options.misconception: A mix of methods is a safe middle ground.

templates.principle: Follow the manufacturer's guidance for tools and equipment, and raise concerns about time openly rather than using unapproved shortcuts.

review.notes: No claims about specific legal requirements.

templates.scenario: A coworker writes this plan before using {equipment|the}.
templates.prompt: Tap the line that is a problem.

segments.text: Before I start, I will read the manufacturer's quick guide.
segments.whyFine: Reading the guide is a good preparation step.

segments.text: I will take off the safety guard because it slows me down.
segments.why: A safety guard is there to protect the user, and removing it for speed is an unsafe shortcut.

segments.text: I will make sure the work area is clear.
segments.whyFine: Keeping the area clear is a sensible precaution.

segments.text: I will ask my lead if I have any questions.

templates.principle: Never remove or bypass a safety guard to save time.

templates.scenario: You are about to use {equipment|the} for a job at {workplace|the}, and you have been trained on it.
templates.prompt: Put these steps in a sensible order.

steps.text: Read the manufacturer's guidance for the tool
Put on the required protective equipment
Clean and store it as directed

precedence.why: You should know the manufacturer's directions before using the tool.
A damaged tool should be found before it is used.
Protective equipment must be on before the tool is in use.
You clean and store the tool after the work is done.

templates.principle: Prepare to use a tool by reading guidance, inspecting it and putting on protection; then use it, and clean and store it as directed.

review.notes: Preparation steps may happen in any order before use; each alternate is professionally sound.

templates.scenario: {Equipment|the} at {workplace|the} was replaced with a newer model that has a different safety lock. Your training covered the older model. Your workplace allows only trained employees to use equipment, and your {lead} wants the job started now.

options.text: Tell your {lead} the model changed, read the manufacturer's guide for the new one, and get a short orientation before using it.
options.why: The new safety lock is different from what you learned. Telling your {lead}, reading the guide and getting oriented fits the rule that only trained people use equipment.

options.text: Read the manufacturer's guide for the new model and begin, without mentioning the change.
options.why: Reading the guide is good, but the workplace allows only trained people to use equipment, and your {lead} does not know your training covered a different model.
options.misconception: If I have read the manual, I am trained.

options.text: Use it the same way as the old one, since the controls look similar and the job needs to start.
options.why: Similar controls do not mean the same safety features. The different lock is exactly where a mistake could injure someone.
options.misconception: Equipment that looks similar works the same way.

options.text: Wait for the next scheduled training session in a few months before using it at all.
options.why: Waiting that long is unnecessary when a short orientation could be arranged now. It also leaves the job without a trained person.
options.misconception: Training only counts if it is the full official session.

templates.principle: When equipment changes, say so, read the guidance for the new model, and get oriented before using it.

review.notes: Workplace rule stated; acceptable option reads the guide but skips communication.
